name: Assistants & copilots
summary: AI built into the places people already work: chat assistants and copilots inside editors, documents and apps.

text: A copilot sits next to the pilot and helps, but the pilot is still in charge.
AI copilots suggest text, code or answers, and you decide what to keep.
D1.analogy: A copilot helping, while the pilot stays in charge.

text: Copilots bring model calls into existing tools: code editors, email, documents and search.
Good designs keep people in control: suggestions appear inline, are easy to accept or reject, and show their sources.
Behind the interface sit the lower layers: an agent or orchestrated calls, a model endpoint, and infrastructure.

layers.label: Orchestration
layers.sub: context from your document or repo

D2.analogy: A copilot helping, while the pilot stays in charge.
D2.analogyBreaks: A human copilot is accountable and consistent. An AI copilot can be confidently wrong in different ways each time, so review matters more, not less.

predict.question: What is the main job of a copilot's interface design?
options: Make suggestions easy to review, accept or reject
Take the user out of the loop
predict.explanation: Keeping a person in the loop with low-friction review is the core pattern.

text: Open questions: measuring real productivity effects, over-reliance and skill loss, and interfaces for agents that take actions rather than make suggestions.

sources.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
